routing_warnings.description: The request to replace the expressive flourish with a restrained architectural terminal primarily changes the independently evolving shared terminal treatment.
The six requested material-quality edge treatments primarily define the shared signature terminal rather than the core Hero V silhouette.
The request for the second V to sit above the E and L while below the Hero V and accent primarily changes vertical hierarchy, not glyph construction.
The second-V clause concerns its vertical position relative to the E, L, Hero V, and accent.
The requested architectural terminal refinement is explicitly shared across the Hero V, second V, and É accent.
The selected terminal profile and requested softness refinements concern the shared terminal treatment rather than the complete second-V geometry.
The literal reuse of the Hero V terminal as the É accent is primarily an accent-derivation rule rather than a change to the terminal profile itself.
The reported loss of an exact Hero V terminal copy in the accent is better routed to the literal accent-derivation Requirement.
The reported loss of the Hero V foundation is a runtime failure of Hero V geometry; only the separate request for softer, non-calligraphic terminal language belongs to the target Requirement.
The request to reduce the E and L scale concerns their compositional scale rather than their architectural letterform construction.
The request for the letterforms to sit on a common baseline belongs to baseline alignment rather than E and L form design.
The requested alignment of E and L height to the second V's left arm concerns cap-height scale.
The primary change is to make the second V a true proportional reduction; the dependent E and L height adjustment belongs to REQ_E_L_CAP_HEIGHT_SCALE.
The requested comparison varies the proportional scale of the second V while holding the E and L letterforms unchanged.
The complaint that the second V was redrawn or changed concerns the locked glyph asset rather than specifically entailing its visual hierarchy.
The statement that the second V is not the approved version concerns glyph identity rather than its relative placement and prominence.
The request for a true proportional reduction of the Hero V primarily changes the second V's construction method; its hierarchy outcome repeats the rule already recorded at message 171.
The change from mathematical scaling to an optically drawn second V primarily changes glyph construction, while retaining the existing supporting hierarchy.
The reported failure is primarily that the approved Hero V geometry changed; the message preserves the alignment rule but does not clearly report a distinct peak-alignment failure.
The client reports that the submitted Hero V is not the approved geometry; this is primarily a Hero V geometry failure.
The client says the Hero V foundation was lost while describing the reference lines as helpful; this does not clearly establish a new peak-alignment failure.
The project-ending failure specifically identifies loss of the locked Hero V and second V hierarchy and geometry, not a distinct failure of Hero V–accent peak alignment.
